title: Vector quantization
authors: Wikipedia contributors, developed by Robert M. Gray (1980s)
distortion_equations: D = Expected squared quantization error (sum of squared differences between input vectors and centroids)
Voronoi partition: each vector assigned to nearest centroid by Euclidean distance
Minimize expected squared quantization error
theoretical_insights: VQ partitions input data space into Voronoi regions where each region is determined by closeness to representation vectors. Uses prototype-based clustering where centroids function as density points. Density matching property ensures compressed data has errors inversely proportional to local density.

title: K-means clustering and vector quantization (scipy.cluster.vq) — SciPy v1.18.0 Manual
distortion_equations: Distortion D = sum of squared distances between observation vectors and dominating centroids
For vector v belonging to cluster i: minimize ∑||x_i - μ_i||²
Codebook: k by N array where row i is centroid of codeword i
Mean squared error (MSE) as distortion measure
clustering_algorithms: Convergence criterion: change in distortion < threshold
theoretical_insights: K-means algorithm minimizes distortion by iteratively reclassifying observations into clusters and recalculating centroids until convergence. The codebook generated can be used to quantize vectors by finding nearest centroid. Information theory terminology: centroid index = 'code', centroid table = 'code book'.

title: TurboQuant: Online Vector Quantization with Near-optimal Distortion Rate
authors: Amir Zandieh, Majid Daliri, Majid Hadian, Vahab Mirrokni
distortion_equations: MSE Distortion: D_mse(Q_mse) = E[||x - Q_mse^(-1)(Q_mse(x))||_2^2] ≤ (√3·π/2)·(1/4^b)
Inner Product Distortion: D_prod(Q_prod) = E[|⟨y,x⟩ - ⟨y,Q_prod^(-1)(Q_prod(x))⟩|²] ≤ (√3·π²·||y||_2²/d)·(1/4^b)
Shannon's source coding distortion-rate function
Lloyd-Max quantizer for scalar quantization optimization
Lower bounds: D_mse(Q) ≥ 1/4^b, D_prod(Q) ≥ ||y||_2²/d·(1/4^b)
clustering_algorithms: Lloyd-Max algorithm for optimal scalar quantizers
theoretical_insights: Vector quantization rooted in Shannon's source coding theory. Random rotation induces Beta distribution on coordinates. Near-independence of coordinates in high dimensions enables per-coordinate scalar quantization while achieving near-optimal distortion. Two-stage approach: MSE-optimal followed by QJL for unbiased inner product estimation. Information-theoretic lower bounds proven; TurboQuant achieves within 2.7x factor of optimality.

title: Differentiable Vector Quantization for Rate-Distortion Optimization of Generative Image Compression
authors: Shiyin Jiang, Wei Long, Minghao Han, Zhenghao Chen, Ce Zhu, Shuhang Gu
distortion_equations: Rate-distortion (RD) optimization framework: minimize D subject to R ≤ R_target
Joint RD optimization for VQ-based compression
Entropy-constrained VQ formulation
Squared error distortion measure D = E[||x - x_hat||²]
clustering_algorithms: VQ codebook learning via entropy modeling
Differentiable soft relaxation of codebook distribution
theoretical_insights: Entropy-constrained vector quantization enables end-to-end rate-distortion optimization. Disconnect between representation learning and entropy modeling solved via differentiable relaxation allowing entropy loss to shape latent prior. VQ achieves strong structural fidelity while maintaining theoretical rate-distortion guarantees.

title: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory: Quantization and Vector Quantization Theory
authors: Robert M. Gray (editor); Lloyd, Max, Linde, Buzo contributions
distortion_equations: Lloyd's optimality conditions for quantizers: necessary conditions any optimal quantizer must satisfy
Minimum distortion quantizer characterization
High-resolution approximations: distortion via Bennett's formula
Vector quantization as block/multidimensional quantization
clustering_algorithms: Lloyd algorithm (Method I) - generalizes to vector quantizers
Lloyd-Max algorithm (Method II, rediscovered by Max 1960)
theoretical_insights: Foundational theory of quantization through Lloyd's optimality conditions. These conditions are necessary for any optimal quantizer achieving minimal distortion. Lloyd's Method I generalizes naturally to vector quantizers (preferred over Method II). High-resolution theory provides upper bounds on minimum distortion for block quantizers of any dimension.

title: Vector Quantization and Clustering - MIT OpenCourseWare Lecture
authors: MIT automatic speech recognition course faculty
distortion_equations: Distortion D = sum of squared distances = ∑_i ||x_i - μ_i||²
Euclidean distance: ||x - μ_i||² = (x - μ_i)^T(x - μ_i)
Normalized dot-product distance: x^T·y / (||x||·||y||)
Weighted Euclidean: (x - μ_i)^T·W·(x - μ_i)
clustering_algorithms: Distance metrics: Euclidean, normalized dot-product, weighted Euclidean
LBG algorithm for codebook design with binary splitting
theoretical_insights: Distance metrics strongly influence cluster shapes. Euclidean distance results in spherical clusters with optimal center being arithmetic mean. Codebook design is critical first step in VQ process. Performance measured by distortion metric or task-relevant metrics like speech recognition accuracy. Robust training minimizes performance degradation between training and testing.
